column1: Canadian writer Jay Ingram investigates the mystery of why leaves turn red in the fall
column2: 加拿大作家杰伊·英格拉姆正在调查树叶在秋季变红之谜。

column1: One of the most captivating natural events of the year in many areas throughout North America is the turning of the leaves in the fall.
column2: 在北美许多地区，秋季树叶变色是一年中最引人注目的自然现象之一。

column1: The colours are magnificent, but the question of exactly why some trees turn yellow or orange, and others red or purple, is something which has long puzzled scientists.
column2: 这些颜色非常壮观，但为什么有些树变成黄色或橙色，而另一些则变成红色或紫色，这个问题长期以来一直困扰着科学家。

column1: Summer leaves are green because they are full of chlorophyll, the molecule that captures sunlight and converts that energy into new building materials for the tree.
column2: 夏天的叶子是绿色的，因为它们富含叶绿素，而叶绿素是一种能够捕捉阳光并将能量转化为树木生长所需物质的分子。

column1: As fall approaches in the northern hemisphere, the amount of solar energy available declines considerably.
column2: 当北半球进入秋季时，可获得的太阳能量会显著减少。

column1: For many trees — evergreen conifers being an exception — the best strategy is to abandon photosynthesis until the spring.
column2: 对许多树木来说（常绿针叶树除外），最佳策略是暂时停止光合作用，直到春天。

column1: So rather than maintaining the now redundant leaves throughout the winter, the tree saves its precious resources and discards them.
column2: 因此，树木不会在冬季保留那些已经不再需要的叶子，而是将宝贵的资源保存下来，同时将其丢弃。

column1: But before letting its leaves go, the tree dismantles their chlorophyll molecules and ships their valuable nitrogen back into the twigs.
column2: 但在落叶之前，树木会分解叶绿素分子，并将宝贵的氮元素重新输送回树枝中。

column1: As chlorophyll is depleted, other colours that have been dominated by it throughout the summer begin to be revealed.
column2: 随着叶绿素的减少，那些在夏季一直被叶绿素所掩盖的其他颜色开始显现出来。

column1: This unmasking explains the autumn colours of yellow and orange, but not the brilliant reds and purples of trees such as the maple or sumac.
column2: 这种暴露解释了秋天树叶呈现黄色和橙色的现象，但无法解释枫树或漆树为何会呈现出鲜艳的红色和紫色。

column1: The source of the red is widely known: it is created by anthocyanins, water-soluble plant pigments reflecting the red to blue range of the visible spectrum.
column2: 红色的来源已经广为人知：它是由花青素这种水溶性植物色素反射可见光谱中红到蓝范围产生的。

column1: They belong to a class of sugar-based chemical compounds also known as flavonoids.
column2: 它们属于一类以糖为基础的化学化合物，这类化合物也被称为黄酮类化合物。

column1: What’s puzzling is that anthocyanins are actually newly minted, made in the leaves at the same time as the tree is preparing to drop them.
column2: 令人困惑的是，花青素实际上是新产生的，是在树木准备落叶时于叶片中同时合成的。

column1: But it is hard to make sense of the manufacture of anthocyanins—why should a tree bother making new chemicals in its leaves when it’s already scrambling to withdraw and preserve the ones already there?
column2: 不过，要理解花青素的生成过程其实相当困难——既然树木已经忙于提取和保存现有的化学物质，那为什么还要在叶片中制造新的化学物质呢？

column1: Some theories about anthocyanins have argued that they might act as a chemical defence against attacks by insects or fungi, or that they might attract fruit-eating birds or increase a leaf’s tolerance to freezing.
column2: 有些关于花青素的理论认为，它们可能起到化学防御作用，抵御昆虫或真菌的侵袭，也可能吸引以果实为食的鸟类，或提高叶片对冰冻的耐受力。
column14: tolerance to freezing|对冰冻的耐受力

column1: However there are problems with each of these theories, including the fact that leaves are red for such a relatively short period that the expense of energy needed to manufacture the anthocyanins would outweigh any anti-fungal or anti-herbivore activity achieved.
column2: 不过，这些理论各有问题。例如，叶片呈红色的时间相对短暂，以至于合成花青素所耗费的能量，会超过它在抵御真菌或植食动物方面带来的任何益处。

column1: It has also been proposed that trees may produce vivid red colours to convince herbivorous insects that they are healthy and robust and would be easily able to mount chemical defences against infestation.
column2: 还有人提出，树木可能会呈现鲜艳的红色，借此让植食性昆虫相信，这些树健康而强壮，能够轻易启动化学防御来抵御虫害。

column1: If insects paid attention to such advertisements, they might be prompted to lay their eggs on a duller, and presumably less resistant host.
column2: 如果昆虫留意到这样的信号，它们就可能转而在颜色较暗淡、抗虫能力想必也较弱的寄主植物上产卵。
column6: be prompted to|受到促使而去做

column1: The flaw in this theory lies in the lack of proof to support it.
column2: 这一理论的缺陷在于缺乏支持它的证据。

column1: No one has as yet ascertained whether more robust trees sport the brightest leaves, or whether insects make choices according to colour intensity.
column2: 目前还没有人能够确定，是那些更健壮的树木才拥有最鲜艳的叶子，还是昆虫是根据叶子的颜色深浅来做出选择的。

column1: Perhaps the most plausible suggestion as to why leaves would go to the trouble of making anthocyanins when they’re busy packing up for the winter is the theory known as the ‘light screen’ hypothesis.
column2: 或许，关于为什么树叶在忙于准备过冬的过程中还要耗费精力来合成花青素的最有道理的解释，就是所谓的‘光屏假说’。

column1: It sounds paradoxical, because the idea behind this hypothesis is that the red pigment is made in autumn leaves to protect chlorophyll, the light-absorbing chemical, from too much light.
column2: 这听起来似乎有些矛盾，因为这一假设的核心是：秋天树叶中产生的红色色素，是为了保护叶绿素这种能吸收光线的化学物质，免受过强光照的损害。

column1: Why does chlorophyll need protection when it is the natural world’s supreme light absorber?
column2: 既然叶绿素是自然界最高效的光吸收者，为什么还需要保护它呢？

column1: Why protect chlorophyll at a time when the tree is breaking it down to salvage as much of it as possible?
column2: 在树木正在分解叶绿素、以尽可能多地回收其成分的时候，为什么还要保护叶绿素呢？

column1: Chlorophyll, although exquisitely evolved to capture the energy of sunlight, can sometimes be overwhelmed by it, especially in situations of drought, low temperatures, or nutrient deficiency.
column2: 叶绿素虽然经过精密的进化，能够捕捉阳光中的能量，但在干旱、低温或营养缺乏的情况下，有时会被过多的阳光能量所淹没。

column1: Moreover, the problem of oversensitivity to light is even more acute in the fall, when the leaf is busy preparing for winter by dismantling its internal machinery.
column2: 而且，在秋季，当树叶忙着拆解其内部机制以应对过冬时，对光线的过度敏感问题变得更加严重。

column1: The energy absorbed by the chlorophyll molecules of the unstable autumn leaf is not immediately channelled into useful products and processes, as it would be in an intact summer leaf.
column2: 不稳定的秋叶中叶绿素分子所吸收的能量，并不会像在完整夏叶中那样，立即转化为有用的物质和能量。

column1: The weakened fall leaf then becomes vulnerable to the highly destructive effects of the oxygen created by the excited chlorophyll molecules.
column2: 那些已经变弱的落叶，就很容易受到由激发状态的叶绿素分子产生的氧气所带来的严重破坏作用。

column1: Even if you had never suspected that this is what was going on when leaves turn red, there are clues out there.
column2: 即使你从未想过树叶变红时究竟发生了什么，但实际上还是有一些线索可以揭示真相的。

column1: One is straightforward: on many trees, the leaves that are the reddest are those on the side of the tree which gets most sun.
column2: 一个原因是直接的：对于多数树木来说，叶子最红的那面是接触阳光最多的那面。

column1: Not only that, but the red is brighter on the upper side of the leaf.
column2: 不仅如此，叶子上表面的红色更鲜艳。

column1: It has also been recognised for decades that the best conditions for intense red colours are dry, sunny days and cool nights, conditions that nicely match those that make leaves susceptible to excess light.
column2: 几十年来，人们已经认识到，产生鲜艳红色的最佳条件是干燥、阳光充足且夜晚凉爽的天气，而这种气候条件恰好也使树叶容易受到过度光照的影响。

column1: And finally, trees such as maples usually get much redder the more north you travel in the northern hemisphere.
column2: 最后，在北半球，越往北方，像枫树这样的树木颜色就会变得越红。

column1: It’s colder there, they’re more stressed, their chlorophyll is more sensitive and it needs more sunblock.
column2: 那里的温度更低，树叶更紧张，叶绿素更敏感，需要更多的防晒保护。

column1: What is still not fully understood, however, is why some trees resort to producing red pigments while others don’t bother, and simply reveal their orange or yellow hues.
column2: 不过，仍然有一些原因尚未被完全理解：为什么有些树木会分泌红色色素，而另一些树木则不会这样做，而是选择呈现橙色或黄色。

column1: Do these trees have other means at their disposal to prevent overexposure to light in autumn?
column2: 这些树木是否有其他方式来避免在秋季受到过多的光照呢？

column1: Their story, though not as spectacular to the eye, will surely turn out to be as subtle and as complex.
column2: 它们的故事虽然不那么引人注目，但结果必然是微妙而复杂的。
